# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Port Nereid for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## Elgin's Folly The survey charts call the world LV-109. Everyone who has lived through a wet season calls it [bold]Elgin's Folly[/bold]. Nobody at the port agrees who Elgin was: a surveyor, a Company accountant or a pilot who put down in the wrong valley. All the stories end the same way, with someone looking at the rain and the jungle and deciding to build here anyway.
## The Joint Venture Port Nereid is not a mining camp that grew a spaceport. It was planned as a crossroads from the first day. The [bold]United Americas Colonial Administration[/bold] and [bold]Weyland-Yutani[/bold] split the charter between them: the Administration holds the colony and its people, the Company holds most of the plant and the freight contracts. Both sides still argue over which of them pays for the drains.
## Water and Air - The port's first trade was water. Ships crossing the Neroid Sector put in to refill tanks and take on cargo, and the pumps have not stopped since. - The [bold]PAEK-500[/bold] heavy atmospheric processor, with its twin fusion engines, keeps the air breathable and the lights on. Its coolant reserves in the west wing are the most guarded rooms in the colony, because a processor that size does not fail quietly. - The International Spaceport and the AC-170 cargo depot made Port Nereid a transit hub. Most of what moves through this part of the sector passes over our landing pads at least once.
## The People Dockers, freight specialists, engineers, atmospherics crews and the miners of the TMCC outpost make up most of the town, with Company staff in the WY office and families in the eastern and western habitation complexes. The [bold]Neroid Sector Policing Authority[/bold] keeps the peace, or tries to, in a town where the Administration, the Company and every passing freight crew each believe they make the rules.
## The Press The Herald started as a noticeboard by the mess hall, where dock and depot crews pinned shift changes and complaints. It became a paper the first time somebody pinned up a story the Company wanted taken down. Nobody took it down, and we have kept pinning since.
